```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5, dpi = 120,
                      fig.keep = "last")
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
library(plotly)
kugou_blue <- "#3D7CC9"
kugou_navy <- "#1F4E79"
kugou_sky <- "#A7C7E7"
kugou_orange <- "#F4A261"

theme_kugou <- theme_minimal(base_family = "sans", base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(family = "sans", face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0, color = "#263B4D"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(family = "sans", size = 8.5, color = "#5B6573", hjust = 0),
    plot.caption = element_text(family = "sans", size = 7.5, color = "#5B6573", hjust = 0),
    axis.title = element_text(family = "sans", size = 9, color = kugou_navy),
    axis.text = element_text(family = "sans", size = 8, color = "#4B5563"),
    legend.title = element_text(family = "sans"),
    legend.text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#E5E7EB", linewidth = .35),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA)
  )
root <- normalizePath("..", mustWork = TRUE)
canonical <- read_csv(file.path(root, "data/processed/kugou_analysis_dataset.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
daily <- canonical |> mutate(chart_date = as.Date(chart_date))
track <- canonical |> distinct(kugou_song_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |> mutate(release_date = as.Date(release_date), duration_min = duration_ms / 60000)
```

# 1. Data Quality and Scope

Data quality is checked before any exploratory figure is produced. This report analyses KuGou Top100 as a standalone dataset. Spotify and Douyin fields are not used. The analysis defines the observation unit clearly, separates actual observations from calendar coverage, retains missing values as missing rather than converting them to zero, and avoids duplicate weighting.

# 2. Data Structure and Quality

```{r structure}
cat(sprintf("**Coverage summary:** %s daily records, %s unique tracks, across %s–%s (%s days).", format(nrow(daily), big.mark = ","), format(n_distinct(track$kugou_song_id), big.mark = ","), min(daily$chart_date), max(daily$chart_date), n_distinct(daily$chart_date)))
```

```{r quality}
quality <- tibble(
  Check = c("Exactly 100 records per day", "Duplicate date-rank pairs", "Missing track IDs", "Missing artist names", "Missing album names", "Missing lyric status"),
  Result = c(all(daily |> count(chart_date) |> pull(n) == 100), daily |> count(chart_date, rank) |> filter(n > 1) |> nrow(), sum(is.na(daily$kugou_song_id) | daily$kugou_song_id == ""), sum(is.na(track$artist_name) | track$artist_name == ""), sum(is.na(track$album_name) | track$album_name == ""), sum(is.na(track$lyrics_status) | track$lyrics_status == ""))
)
kable(quality, format = "html", align = c("l", "r"), table.attr = 'class="kugou-table compact-table"')
```

Each row is interpreted as one track-date chart observation. An absent track is not recoded as zero popularity, and `time_on_chart` is treated as observed chart persistence within this archive rather than an official lifetime measure. Because the KuGou Top100 is complete for every date, an additional observation-density figure would be redundant; turnover and persistence are more informative.

The report then examines how the KuGou Top100 changes over time, which music genres dominate the chart, whether ranking performance differs across genres, and how long songs remain visible. The selected figures focus on chart turnover, genre composition, genre-level ranking performance, and chart persistence. Cross-platform overlap, temporal Jaccard, and first-observed timing are reserved for the later integrated analysis because they require Douyin data.

# 3. Data Coverage and Chart Turnover

```{r flow, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
first_date <- min(daily$chart_date)
daily_flow <- daily |> filter(chart_date > first_date) |> group_by(chart_date) |> summarise(new_entries = sum(is.na(pre_rank) | pre_rank == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
monthly_flow <- daily_flow |> mutate(month = floor_date(chart_date, "month")) |> group_by(month) |> summarise(mean_new_entries = mean(new_entries), .groups = "drop")
p_daily <- ggplot(daily_flow, aes(chart_date, new_entries)) + geom_line(color = kugou_blue, linewidth = .55) + geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = kugou_orange, linewidth = .8) + geom_point(data = daily_flow |> slice_max(new_entries, n = 1), color = kugou_orange, size = 2) + geom_text(data = daily_flow |> slice_max(new_entries, n = 1), aes(label = paste0("Peak: ", new_entries)), nudge_y = 3, color = kugou_navy, size = 3.2, family = "sans") + labs(title = "Daily New Songs Number Entering the KuGou Top100", x = "Chart date", y = "Number of new songs") + theme_kugou
p_month <- ggplot(monthly_flow, aes(month, mean_new_entries, fill = mean_new_entries)) + geom_col(width = 25) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FAD7B1", high = kugou_orange, guide = "none") + geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_new_entries, 1)), vjust = -0.35, size = 2.8, color = "#A94F3B") + labs(title = "Average Daily Number of New Songs by Month", x = "Month", y = "Average new songs per day") + theme_kugou + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
turnover_plot <- p_daily / p_month + plot_layout(heights = c(1.45, 1))
turnover_plot
```

The KuGou chart changes continuously, but most days introduce only a small number of new songs. The monthly averages show that turnover varies across the observation period, indicating that chart entry activity is not constant over time.

## Interactive View: Daily Chart Turnover

The daily turnover series is presented as an interactive chart. Hovering shows the exact date and number of new entries; users can zoom, pan, and reset the view. The remaining distributional figures stay static because interactivity adds limited value to those summaries.

```{r daily-interactive, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.5}
daily_interactive <- plot_ly(
  daily_flow,
  x = ~chart_date,
  y = ~new_entries,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",
  line = list(color = kugou_blue, width = 2),
  hovertemplate = paste("Date: %{x|%Y-%m-%d}<br>New entries: %{y}<extra></extra>"),
  width = 1100,
  height = 460
) |>
  add_lines(
    x = daily_flow$chart_date,
    y = predict(loess(new_entries ~ as.numeric(chart_date), data = daily_flow)),
    line = list(color = kugou_orange, width = 2),
    name = "Smoothed trend",
    hoverinfo = "skip"
  ) |>
  layout(
    title = list(text = "Daily New Songs Entering the KuGou Top100", x = 0.02),
    xaxis = list(title = "Chart date", rangeslider = list(visible = TRUE)),
    yaxis = list(title = "New entries (songs)"),
    hovermode = "x unified",
    plot_bgcolor = "white",
    paper_bgcolor = "white",
    font = list(family = "Arial", color = "#263B4D")
  )
daily_interactive
```

# 4. Music Characteristics

```{r genre}
genre_summary <- track |> count(genre_harmonized, name = "tracks") |> arrange(desc(tracks)) |> slice_head(n = 10)
genre_summary <- genre_summary |> mutate(genre = genre_harmonized)
genre_plot <- ggplot(genre_summary, aes(reorder(genre, tracks), tracks, fill = tracks)) + geom_col(width = .7) + scale_fill_gradient(low = kugou_sky, high = kugou_navy, guide = "none") + geom_text(aes(label = paste0(tracks, " tracks")), hjust = -.15, family = "sans", size = 3, color = kugou_navy) + coord_flip() + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .14))) + labs(title = "Music Genre Composition of the KuGou Top100", x = "Music genre", y = "Number of unique tracks") + theme_kugou
genre_plot
```

The chart is concentrated in a small number of genre categories. This shows that the KuGou Top100 has a clear genre composition rather than an even distribution across all classified music types.

# 4. Chart Performance: Peak Rank by Genre
```{r rank-genre, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
genre_long <- track |> select(kugou_song_id, peak_rank, genre_harmonized) |> rename(genre = genre_harmonized)
genre_long <- genre_long |> add_count(genre, name = "genre_n") |> filter(genre_n >= 5)
genre_medians <- genre_long |> group_by(genre) |> summarise(median_rank = median(peak_rank, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
genre_long <- genre_long |> left_join(genre_medians, by = "genre")
rank_genre_plot <- ggplot(genre_long, aes(reorder(genre, peak_rank, FUN = median), peak_rank, fill = median_rank)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = .72, color = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = reorder(genre, peak_rank, FUN = median), y = peak_rank), inherit.aes = FALSE, width = .16, fill = "white", color = kugou_navy, outlier.color = kugou_blue, outlier.alpha = .35) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#7FC6C3", high = kugou_blue, guide = "none") +
  coord_flip() + scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = expansion(mult = c(.05, .18))) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Best Chart Rank by Music Genre", x = "Music genre", y = "Best chart rank (lower rank is better)") + theme_kugou
rank_genre_plot
```

Best-rank performance differs across genres. The violin shapes and boxplots show both differences in central ranking and variation within genres; therefore, genre is useful for explaining ranking performance rather than only describing chart composition.

# 5. Mood Characteristics
```{r theme}
theme_summary <- track |> count(mood_grouped, name = "tracks") |> arrange(desc(tracks))
theme_summary <- theme_summary |> mutate(theme = mood_grouped)
mood_plot <- ggplot(theme_summary, aes(reorder(theme, tracks), tracks, fill = tracks)) + geom_col(width = .7) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FAD7B1", high = "#D96C4F", guide = "none") + geom_text(aes(label = paste0(tracks, " tracks")), hjust = -.15, family = "sans", size = 3, color = "#A94F3B") + coord_flip() + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .14))) + labs(title = "Mood Composition of KuGou Top100 Songs", x = "Music mood", y = "Number of unique tracks") + theme_kugou
mood_plot
```

Genre and mood use harmonized categories for cross-platform comparison: six broad genre groups and six grouped mood categories. The original detailed categories remain in `genre_category` and `mood_category`. KuGou categories are rule-assisted screening results rather than native KuGou labels; interpretations should consider `taxonomy_review_required`.

# 6. Track Profile: Duration

```{r duration}
duration_median <- median(track$duration_min, na.rm = TRUE)
duration_p95 <- quantile(track$duration_min, .95, na.rm = TRUE)
duration_plot <- ggplot(track, aes(duration_min, fill = after_stat(count))) + geom_histogram(binwidth = .25, color = "white") + scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FAD7B1", high = "#D96C4F", guide = "none") + geom_vline(xintercept = duration_median, linetype = "dashed", color = "#A94F3B", linewidth = .7) + geom_vline(xintercept = duration_p95, linetype = "dotted", color = kugou_navy, linewidth = .7) + annotate("text", x = duration_median, y = Inf, label = paste0("Median: ", round(duration_median, 2), " min"), vjust = 1.5, hjust = -.05, color = "#A94F3B", size = 3, family = "sans") + annotate("text", x = duration_p95, y = Inf, label = paste0("95th pct: ", round(duration_p95, 2), " min"), vjust = 3, hjust = 1.05, color = kugou_navy, size = 3, family = "sans") + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, quantile(track$duration_min, .99, na.rm = TRUE))) + labs(title = "Distribution of Song Durations in the KuGou Top100", x = "Song duration (minutes)", y = "Number of unique tracks") + theme_kugou
duration_plot
```

# 7. Chart Persistence

```{r persistence}
persistence_median <- median(track$time_on_chart, na.rm = TRUE)
persistence_max <- max(track$time_on_chart, na.rm = TRUE)
# Retain the original-scale version for reference; it is not printed in the main report.
persistence_plot_original <- ggplot(track, aes(time_on_chart, fill = after_stat(count))) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, color = "white") + scale_fill_gradient(low = "#D6ECDC", high = "#3E9F7D", guide = "none") + labs(title = "How Long Songs Remain in the KuGou Top100 (Original Scale)", x = "Observed days on chart", y = "Number of unique tracks") + theme_kugou

# The main version uses log1p on the x-axis to reveal the dense short-persistence region
# while retaining the long right tail. Labels are shown on the original day scale.
persistence_breaks <- c(1, 3, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 180, 365, persistence_max)
persistence_plot <- track |>
  mutate(persistence_log = log1p(time_on_chart)) |>
  ggplot(aes(persistence_log, fill = after_stat(count))) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = .25, color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#D6ECDC", high = "#3E9F7D", guide = "none") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log1p(persistence_median), linetype = "dashed", color = "#287A61", linewidth = .7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log1p(persistence_max), linetype = "dotted", color = kugou_navy, linewidth = .7) +
  annotate("text", x = log1p(persistence_median), y = Inf, label = paste0("Median: ", persistence_median, " days"), vjust = 1.5, hjust = -.05, color = "#287A61", size = 3, family = "sans") +
  annotate("text", x = log1p(persistence_max), y = Inf, label = paste0("Max: ", persistence_max, " days"), vjust = 3, hjust = 1.05, color = kugou_navy, size = 3, family = "sans") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = log1p(persistence_breaks), labels = persistence_breaks) +
  labs(title = "How Long Songs Remain in the KuGou Top100", x = "Observed days on chart (log1p display; labels show original days)", y = "Number of unique tracks") +
  theme_kugou
persistence_plot
```

Most songs remain in the KuGou Top100 for a relatively short period, while a smaller group stays for much longer. The long right tail identifies persistent chart songs, which can be used in later analysis of the characteristics associated with long-term visibility.

The log1p x-axis is used only for visual display. All persistence summaries and later calculations remain on the original day scale.

```{r longest}
longest <- track |> arrange(desc(time_on_chart), peak_rank) |> select(track_name, artist_name, peak_rank, time_on_chart) |> slice_head(n = 15)
kable(longest, caption = "Tracks with the longest observed Top100 persistence", format = "html", align = c("l", "l", "r", "r"), table.attr = 'class="kugou-table compact-table"')
```

# 8. Preliminary Findings and Limitations

```{r findings, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf("- The data cover %s to %s: %d days, %d daily chart records, and %d unique tracks.\n", min(daily$chart_date), max(daily$chart_date), n_distinct(daily$chart_date), nrow(daily), n_distinct(track$kugou_song_id)))
cat(sprintf("- The median peak rank is %.0f; median observed chart persistence is %.0f days; the maximum is %.0f days.\n", median(track$peak_rank, na.rm = TRUE), median(track$time_on_chart, na.rm = TRUE), max(track$time_on_chart, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat("- Because a complete Top100 is available each day, the daily mean rank has limited variation; new entries, Top10 frequency, peak rank, and persistence are more informative.\n")
cat("- Genre and mood assignments are rule-assisted screening variables with classification risk; this report describes distributions and associations, not causal effects.\n")
```
